newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horizon EGM accepts lower forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Horizon EGM accepts lower forecasts.

text.p: Shareholders at Hungarian pharmaceuticals research and development company Horizon-Multiplan on Thursday accepted the company's revised forecast which adjusted downwards earlier profit predictions.
"The shareholders accepted the revised plan in its entirety," chairman of the board Janos Pogany told Reuters by phone after an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.
The revised plan predicts a pre-tax loss of 80 million forints, instead of an original forecast of a 43 million forint profit.
Pogany said the company had fallen short of its 1996 sales target of 240,000 units of its sole product Humet-R -- a health supplement containing trace elements.
"Unfortunately we expect to sell only 160,000 to 170,000 bottles," he said.

A further disappointment was the failure to sign a contract for deliveries to Russia of 300,000 bottles of Humet-R. "Unfortunately this has not yet been concluded so I'm afraid we can only deliver 40,000 this year," Pogany said.

Creditanstalt Securities (CA) in October rated Horizon as a "sell," saying the share was overvalued. However, the CA report and poor results have not affected the company's share price, which on Thursday stood at 265 forints, a year high first reached on November 15.
"We were a little bit surprised that after we published our unfavuorable results the price didn't go down," Pagony said.
He added he believed the company had turned the corner, with the Russian contract still on the cards with November producing a profit.
"We've introduced basic changes such as dispensing with an agent to distribute our product in Hungary," he said.
"A promotional campaign we launched in September, while not up to our expectations, has also had a beneficial effect," Pogany added.
